aside.question: Is the eyepiece the top lens?

narration: Let's work out magnification. A microscope makes an image bigger than the real thing. Magnification tells you how many times larger the image appears than the real object. It has no unit, and it is written with a multiplication sign, for example times four hundred. The eyepiece lens has its own magnification, often times ten. So does the objective lens, for example times forty. The two lenses work together, so their magnifications are multiplied. Ten times forty gives four hundred. Not fifty: the two magnifications are multiplied, never added. You can also work out the magnification of a drawing or photograph. Magnification equals image size divided by actual size. Rearranged, actual size equals image size divided by magnification. Here is one. A student's drawing of a cheek cell is forty-eight millimetres wide, and the magnification of the drawing is times eight hundred. Forty-eight divided by eight hundred is nought point nought six millimetres. Cells are so small that their actual size is better given in micrometres. One millimetre is one thousand micrometres, so multiply by one thousand. The cell is sixty micrometres wide.
